evidence_quotes.agenda: "Do you have any special instructions, concerns [or] stresser about moving in general that you want me to take note of at this time?" — asked after rooms/items/boxes/packing/second-address probing was already done
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: "I basically just need [help] because of the weight and the labor of the boxes and busing them up and down the stairs. Because it's just me. So I can't do it on my own" — a real concern acknowledged ("Understood, of course") with an immediate straight pivot into the pricing pitch, no follow-up question
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "if the move itself... takes shorter than the nine hours, that's fine, you only pay for how long it's gonna take" (window) + "we only charge in fifteen minute increments" (beats-it-pay-less) — two of five lines present

top_strength: Clean, specific long-distance estimate breakdown — separated hourly time, travel fee, and overnight fee clearly so the customer understood exactly what she was paying for.
coaching_note: Real, named concern ("it's just me, I can't do it on my own") got acknowledged and dropped instead of followed up — this is exactly the zero-credit pattern the rubric calls out (concern raised, straight pivot to pricing, no second layer); worth flagging as the single highest-leverage fix on this call.
